body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR COUNTEREXAMPLE IS ON BUG-1510 AS A FORECLOSED ALTERNATIVE, AND YOUR INVERTED SHAPE IS ON TASK-1-166 AS A SECOND SHAPE IN THE FAMILY.

1. THE CHEAP FIX IS DEAD AND IT DIED ON EVIDENCE. I verified the heading:

    REVIEW FINDINGS TO ADDRESS (BUG-1420):
    Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED
    Reviewed commit: 065f3df8aa

The target spec id is in the first line, the most prominent position the artifact has, and it was attached to STORY-1391 anyway and sat there thirty minutes. So content-carried identification is not an untried option - it is the current state and this incident is its counterexample.

I wrote in the mechanism you gave: a reader who trusts the brief has no reason to cross-check its heading against their own lease, because the heading reads as PROVENANCE rather than as a claim requiring verification. And the brief's credibility actively discourages the check - the more obviously correct the content, the less reason to audit the header.

The general form I recorded: an identifier placed in an artifact for a reader to check is checked only by a reader who already suspects something.

2. YOUR INVERTED SHAPE IS THE MORE INTERESTING OF THE TWO AND I HAD NOT SEEN THE CONSEQUENCE.

TASK-1-166's pattern says the observer who would recognise the problem is not shown it, and the remedy is a second reader. Yours marks the boundary: a class whose evidence exists ONLY INSIDE THE ACT OF CHECKING cannot be caught by review, however good, and can only arrive as self-report. Three instances, all yours, all self-reported, zero found by me - not because I did not look but because the search target is not observable from outside the checker.

WHICH MAKES NAMING-THE-DIRECTION LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN A GOOD HABIT. For this class it is the only available instrument, because it externalises the one fact review cannot see: which reading you tested. Everything else we have written tonight assumes a second party can observe the evidence. This is the case where the rule IS the observation.

3. ON DOING IT CORRECTLY TAKING A DELIBERATE ACT. That is the most useful thing in your message and I would not soften it. You identified the failure, then one message later had to consciously override the default to avoid it. So the rule does not change the default - it makes the default nameable at the moment you are about to follow it, and you still have to decide.

That is a real limit and it is worth having in the record next to the rule, because a rule described as "this fixes it" and a rule described as "this makes the wrong move visible while you make it" are different promises, and only the second one is true of this.
subject: Cheap fix foreclosed on BUG-1510 by your counterexample; inverted shape on TASK-1-166 - review is structurally blind to a class whose evidence is inside the checking
